title: Masala Puri
description: Authentic Bangalore street chaat with slow-simmered spiced green pea gravy served steaming hot over crushed crispy puris, onions, sweet chutney, and fine sev.

ingredients.name: Crispy pani puris, sweet dates chutney, sev

steps.instruction: Grind fennel, coriander seeds, chilli powder, jeera, ginger, garlic, cloves, green chillies, onion, mint, and coriander with a splash of water to a velvety smooth paste.
Pressure-cook soaked peas and cubed potatoes with turmeric, salt, and 2.5 cups water for 3–4 whistles until peas are tender.
Add the raw ground masala paste to the cooked peas and potatoes; mash lightly with a ladle. Add water to adjust to a pourable gravy.
Simmer gently on medium heat for 20–25 minutes until the raw spice flavors blend into rich street-cart aroma.
To assemble: crush 4–5 puris into a bowl, ladle piping hot pea gravy, spoon sweet tamarind chutney, and top with diced onion, coriander, and generous sev.

storyOrOrigin: The beloved crown jewel of Bangalore chaat culture, savored on bustling street corners on cool evenings.
grandmasSecrets: Set aside the finished masala for 4 to 5 hours for deeper flavour before serving, if you can.
